scope: Active application, GA4, Vercel, database-trigger, and Supabase Edge Function analytics emissions in src/, supabase/functions/, and supabase/migrations/.
environmentPolicy: Browser GA4, Vercel Analytics, and first-party client RPCs are allowed only on resumeats.cv/www.resumeats.cv and outside /admin routes; explicit granted analytics consent is also required.

eventSources.trigger: Consent-granted pathname change; query strings are omitted.
eventSources.deduplication: Suppresses repeat pathname values for the mounted component; no event key.

eventSources.trigger: Analytics component mounts on allowlisted Vercel hostnames.
Checkout button handler begins, before the provider request succeeds.
eventSources.consent: Both GA4 and the authenticated first-party RPC require granted consent on an allowed production customer route.
eventSources.deduplication: First-party client event key is random per call; repeated clicks are distinct events.

eventSources.trigger: Customer presses a provider checkout button; this records intent before the provider request and does not claim checkout success.
eventSources.consent: Requires explicit granted consent on an allowed production customer route.
eventSources.deduplication: Random client event key per accepted click; repeated attempts remain distinct. GA4 begin_checkout is emitted separately only after checkout creation succeeds.

eventSources.trigger: Provider checkout URL/session was created successfully, immediately before redirect.
eventSources.deduplication: No client event key; a repeated successful initiation may emit again.

eventSources.trigger: A new email identity is returned by Supabase Auth.
eventSources.consent: Requires granted consent; sends only method=email.
eventSources.deduplication: No client event key. First-party account_created is independently captured by the user-row trigger.

eventSources.trigger: Only after the page receives a successful server verification response; it is not emitted on redirect parameters alone.
eventSources.deduplication: Uses the provider-prefixed opaque UUID of the server-recorded purchase event as transaction_id; raw Stripe/PayPal identifiers remain server-side. Paid invoice/transaction keys deduplicate webhook and verification retries. Google documents purchase de-duplication for the same transaction_id on web streams; processed production behavior still needs verification.

eventSources.trigger: Stripe webhook or verified Stripe/PayPal subscription outcome.
eventSources.consent: Server-side operational event; separate from optional browser analytics consent.
eventSources.deduplication: Stable paid invoice/transaction key; duplicate-key retries return the same opaque analytics event UUID. Stripe emits only after a positive paid invoice; PayPal keys each verified completed billing transaction separately.

eventSources.trigger: A Stripe session or PayPal subscription checkout is successfully created.
eventSources.consent: Server-side operational event; separate from optional browser analytics consent.

eventSources.deduplication: Stable account UUID event key; conflict is ignored.
Stable resume UUID event key; conflict is ignored.

eventSources.trigger: After a successful application insert, the client helper emits status-only GA4 when consent is granted; the database trigger records the first-party event after insert.
eventSources.consent: GA4 requires explicit granted consent on an allowed production customer route; first-party capture is database-triggered.
eventSources.deduplication: First-party capture uses a stable application UUID event key; GA4 emits once per successful client insert and does not send application content or identifiers.

eventSources.trigger: The six export-success callsites run after PDF/DOCX generation and download dispatch succeeds; browser completion does not prove the user retained or read the file.
eventSources.consent: Both destinations require granted consent on an allowed production customer route; exports only the format.
eventSources.deduplication: First-party event uses a random event key per successful export; repeated exports remain distinct. GA4 has no event key.

eventSources.trigger: Authenticated support start/resolve action with a conversation ID.
eventSources.consent: Server-side first-party event; best-effort and does not block support.

eventSources.trigger: Authenticated customer provider operation; completion follows valid provider output, while failures use fixed safe categories.
eventSources.consent: Requires the client’s explicit granted preference plus a production ResumeATS origin; otherwise no lifecycle event is written.
eventSources.deduplication: Attempt UUID plus lifecycle event name; stores only feature/provider/allowlisted model, duration, usage version, and safe failure code. Prompt, resume, job, email, answer, and provider-response content are never recorded; cost_version is explicitly unpriced.

unwiredOrMissing: Repeated GA4 purchase dispatch from a return-page retry is left to documented web-stream transaction_id deduplication using an opaque analytics event UUID; verify processed production reports and ensure IDs remain unique per provider transaction.
support-ai-worker keeps separate operational usage records and is not included in the consent-gated ai_generation lifecycle event family.
This manifest describes source wiring, not production deployment, event delivery, consented traffic, or processed GA4/first-party event counts.

verification.purpose: Checks aggregate callsite counts for known analytics helper APIs and verifies direct emitter/trigger source markers so new callsites require a manifest update.
